title: Ms. O'Hara — strapping, the helmet, shock treatment again
status: made once (no audition) — possible redo: Sophie's face landed on the female nurse
text:
Sophie peeks through the doorway in her room, pausing to watch the commotion outside her door. 

There is an older woman who has short brown hair in a wild mess at the top of her head. She is adorned in the blue pajamas that all of the patients wear and she is holding her arms perfectly straight and still at her side while two nurses, one on either side, buckle the straps to the stretcher they are wheeling her on. On her head she wears a metal helmet with many little wires hanging off of it. The wires are red and blue and gold. 

“They say I have to get shock treatment again,” she says to no one in particular. 
"I don’t mind the treatment, I’m just worried about what it will do to my memory. 


The doctor said I might not remember everything once I’ve had it,” she says, looking worried indeed. She points her face up at one of the nurses so he is forced to make eye contact with her. “Yees.” he says encouragingly, “To help your miiind Ms. O’Hara. To help you stop having those visions.” he draws out the word mind as if she might not quite undersand if he doesn’t.

title: Ms. O'Hara — ghosts and goblins, ready to be wheeled
status: waits for: Ms. O'Hara's audition (needs your words for her and the two nurses)
text:
“Oh yes,” she says, her face still screwed up with dread. “The world is a very dismal place, isn’t it? There are all these ghosts and goblins” she says, and her speech begins to waver and get faster at the same time, “and they’re always trying to get me!”

“Shh Shh Ms. O’Hara. After your treatment, you’ll feel muuch better.” says the same male nurse. “Now we’ll just wheel you to the treatment room. 

Are you ready to be wheeled, Ms. O’Hara?” 
The woman nods, closing her eyes as they well with tears. She moves her hand to brush them away but it’s now fully strapped to the gurney and it simply falls limp at her side.

title: Walking beside the stretcher — be a good girl and go back to your room
status: waits for: Ms. O'Hara's audition (needs your words for her and the two nurses)
text:
Sophie leaves her room as they begin wheeling her down the hallway, walking next to the stretcher as they wheel it down the hallway, turning her head sideways so she can look at the face of the woman which is screwed up in fear, a tear burrowing its way down the side of her face. “What are they doing to you?” says Sophie in a slight whisper, and the woman looks up in surprise.

“Sophie! Be a good girl and go back to your room. There’s no use being in other people’s business,” says the female nurse who has yet to speak. Sophie stops walking next to the stretcher, looking onsadly as it disapears through the double doors at the end of the hallway.

title: The end of the hallway — take the pill / don't take the pill
status: ready — the door with no handle (a possible ending)
text: She sits at the end of the hallway, next to the hallway which patients go in as they choose. It’s never been locked so long as she’s been there but there is no handle on the inside of the door. mulling over the matter of whether or not to take the pill she’s been prescribed. “Take the pill,” she mutters, clenching her fists tightly, then releasing, and the antithesis: “Don’t take the pill,” she clenches her fists again. She repeats these two phrases eleven times in a row before screwing up her eyes in concentration as though the decision were laid out in front of her and she has just to interpret it in order to know what to do. She gives up and resorts to clenching her fists again, muttering those words over and over so it sounds like a mantra.
